Myths on Clay retells the traditions of the Māori of Aotearoa New Zealand in the style of kōwhaiwhai, the painted rafter patterns of the meeting house. These are living traditions: every iwi (tribe) tells them in its own way, and we always say which written version we follow. Our patterns are drawn for the show and copy no real carving or tā moko.
Sources: Sir George Grey, Polynesian Mythology (1855), largely from the writings of Wiremu Maihi Te Rangikāheke of Te Arawa; John White, The Ancient History of the Maori (1887–1890); Elsdon Best, Maori Religion and Mythology (1924); Te Rangi Hīroa (Sir Peter Buck), The Coming of the Maori (1949). Further reading: Margaret Orbell, The Illustrated Encyclopedia of Māori Myth and Legend; Te Ara, the Encyclopedia of New Zealand.
Narrated by Matías.
